currentContext.strengths: Experienced promoters and agile leadership|Digital-led automation and customer intelligence|Advanced manufacturing and technical capabilities|R&D focused on innovation and sustainability|Diverse, versatile product portfolio (3,000+ products)|Growth supported by strategic acquisitions|Extensive pan-India distribution network|Strong customer loyalty and focus|Sustainability-led competitive edge
currentContext.strategies: AHN division executed a major strategic pivot in 2025-26: transitioning from a fragmented, distributor-led retail model to a focused key-account model targeting large poultry farmers, feed millers and select aqua accounts.|Institutional and Consumer businesses undergoing rigorous review and structural optimisation — pruning low-margin, high-working-capital segments to redirect capital towards the high-return specialty chemicals core.|Pet Care strategy (built on the Lozalo brand) aligns with premiumisation and value-added solutions rather than volume growth, leveraging AHN enzyme/probiotic/herbal-extract expertise.|Shifting from a centralised export model to a localised, regional-hub supply chain — Thailand blending unit for Southeast Asia, proposed KSA facility for MENA — to reduce exposure to geopolitical and logistics disruption.|In Personal Care, the Company is moving up the value chain from bulk phenoxyethanol supply to proprietary, high-margin preservative blend platforms integrated deeper into customer formulations.|Building regulatory readiness in Pharma to scale high-purity excipients, PEGs, pharma coating polymers and esters, transitioning from volume-led supply to value-led partnerships.|In TSC, capturing the full fibre-to-fabric value chain via a technical-service model, with technical teams deployed directly on customers' factory floors for process troubleshooting and application support.|Systematic process innovation: transitioning from traditional batch manufacturing to Continuous Flow Chemistry to reduce reaction times, energy consumption and cost, while supporting sustainability.|R&D strategy centred on the Rossari Global Research & Innovation Centre (GRIC), evolving from a formulation-led approach to broader, scalable multi-vertical platform technologies (e.g., biosurfactants such as sophorolipids).|Board-stated strategic priorities: geographic expansion across core divisions, launch of novel products in key chemistries (surfactants, phenoxy series, performance chemicals), and strengthening partnerships to increase wallet share.|Strategic steps across capacity expansion, portfolio development, customer relationships, exports and international initiatives are intended to accelerate growth over the next 2-3 years through disciplined execution.|The Company has adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy under Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations, establishing the parameters the Board considers before declaring or recommending dividend; the Policy explicitly excludes bonus share issuance and buybacks and is not a substitute for the Board's own judgement, which weighs all relevant circumstances at the time. Governance philosophy is framed around transparency, fairness, accountability, sustainability and integrity, with a stated aim of expanding the definition of success beyond profit to societal and environmental contributions.
currentContext.expansion: Rossari's FY26 capex programme centred on the Dahej cluster: an additional 20,000 MTPA capacity expansion at Dahej was commissioned effective 26th September 2025, taking total installed capacity to 2,72,500 MTPA (Directors' Report), while a 30,000 MTPA ethoxylation facility at Unitop's Dahej facility was commissioned in a phased manner across September 2025 and March 2026 and is in steady ramp-up, with fungible reactors being used to scale non-EO product lines amid near-term Ethylene Oxide supply constraints. Across the group, the Company capitalised approximately Rs 2,445 million during 2025-26 towards this capacity augmentation, funded through a mix of internal accruals and debt; the new Thailand blending unit was funded the same way. Internationally, the Company received in-principle approval to set up a greenfield manufacturing facility in KSA, strengthening regional access, supply-chain resilience and speed-to-market, subject to funding evaluation and statutory approvals. Manufacturing is spread across six named facilities — Dahej I (1,52,500 MTPA, 23 acres), Dahej II (90,000 MTPA, 22 acres), Silvassa (1,20,000 MTPA, 9 acres), Sarigam (15,000 MTPA, 2.5 acres), Vasai (600 MTPA, 0.27 acres) and Thailand (5,000 MTPA, 0.46 acres). With major capacity creation now in place, management's stated focus is shifting from capacity creation to capital efficiency — better asset utilisation, improved asset turns and integration-led efficiencies, supported by SAP S/4HANA and Salesforce.
currentContext.mdna: The global specialty chemicals industry is undergoing structural transformation driven by supply chain realignments, geopolitical shifts, stringent regulatory frameworks and an accelerating sustainable-chemistry mandate.|2025-26 was marked by geopolitical tensions, Red Sea logistics disruptions and freight fluctuations; textile tariff pressures led to cautious buying behaviour and strict collateral requirements from international buyers.|Global conglomerates are aggressively de-risking supply chains, seeking partners offering backward integration and structural feedstock reliability.|End-consumer habits are shifting rapidly — e.g. rising washing-machine penetration is driving a structural shift from powder to liquid detergents in home care; rising global meat consumption is accompanied by stricter food-safety demands in animal health.|B2B customers increasingly require complex, proprietary blends and regulatory-compliant ingredients rather than commoditised single molecules.|Global tariffs are pressuring margins for textile exporters and FMCG manufacturers, and customers are demanding 'chemistry plus service' — solutions that optimise the entire manufacturing cycle, not isolated chemical inputs.|Customers (global FMCG and industrial brands) are seeking bio-based, zero-effluent and sustainable alternatives rather than merely passing environmental audits.|International business contributed about 26% of consolidated revenue in FY26, growing 11% YoY, driven by deeper engagement with existing customers and expansion in Latin America, Europe, Southeast Asia and Africa.|FY26 consolidated revenue growth of 15% was supported by healthy traction across businesses and steady progress in international markets, with all key divisions delivering healthy growth despite raw-material volatility and geopolitical disruption.

risks.note: Fluctuations in the prices of critical chemical inputs directly impact profit margins and overall profitability; mitigated by diversifying raw material sources/supply chains and investing in alternative sustainable 'green' raw materials.

Tariffs on textile exports to the U.S. created demand pressures for domestic customers and direct exports, resulting in pricing constraints and margin pressure; mitigated by diversifying customer base/geographic markets and growing exports to Europe, Southeast Asia and the Middle East.

Entry of new players or low-cost international producers threatens market share and pricing power; mitigated through continuous innovation, differentiated high-value specialty products and operational efficiency/cost optimisation.

Stricter global regulations on chemical safety and sustainability increase compliance costs and potential penalties; mitigated by adopting 'Green Chemistry' and environmentally benign substitutes for legacy harmful products.

Geopolitical tensions or logistical challenges such as freight cost spikes can impact production and timely delivery; mitigated by robust supply chain risk management and establishing international formulation hubs (Thailand and KSA) to improve speed-to-market.

Near-term EO supply constraints affect the HPPC division's ethoxylation throughput; the Company is leveraging fungible reactors to scale non-EO product lines and pivoting towards green chemistry/biosurfactants to mitigate this dependency.
The Company's debt-to-equity ratio increased year-on-year due to additional borrowings taken during the year, partly to fund capacity expansion.

one-line thesis: Highest-ever quarterly revenue (INR 697.2 cr, +28% YoY) and EBITDA (INR 80.6 cr, +18.7%) — but **margin, not growth, is the whole story**: consol EBITDA margin slipped to 11.6% (from 12.5% YoY) dragged by the loss-making institutional/B2C tail, RM/freight volatility (a one-off ~INR 5 cr phenol hit) and seeding costs (Thailand, KSA). The bull case is a self-help margin ladder: exit B2C (frees 2–3% EBITDA), monetise non-core real estate (Andheri office sold this Q), ramp under-utilised capacity (MDEA/ethoxylation), and scale higher-margin pharma/aroma — targeting ~15%+ steady-state consol EBITDA in ~2 years. Management keeps the FY27 top-line guide conservative at **~15%** despite the 28% Q1, citing war/freight/EO-supply uncertainty.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q1FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | INR 697.2 cr | +28% | highest ever; volume +10%, rest price |
| EBITDA | INR 80.6 cr | +18.7% | highest ever; margin 11.6% (vs 12.5% YoY) |
| Core B2B EBITDA (ex instl/B2C) | INR 85 cr | +13% | ~14% margin — the "real" business |
| PAT | INR 35.1 cr | +4.5% | lagging EBITDA on higher interest/depreciation |
| Segment growth | HPPC / TSC / AHN each ~+28% | — | HPPC crossed INR 550 cr quarterly |
| Exports | ~INR 160 cr (23–24% of rev) | +20–21% | mix steady 23–25% |
| Net debt | INR 248 cr | vs INR 280 cr (Mar) | modestly down |
| Interest cost | ~INR 11 cr | rising | capitalised CAPEX term-loans now in P&L; run-rate → INR 9–10 cr/qtr |
| Other income | INR 3.2 cr | — | only profit element of Andheri office sale (~INR 10.5 cr gross) |
> Margin call-outs: institutional + consumer/B2C business is **flat YoY and loss-making** — the main consol-margin drag (its EBITDA-per-kg optics distorted). One-off ~INR 5 cr **phenol** hit (delayed China shipment forced spot buying); one RM block-buy mistimed. Base/core-B2B margin already ~14–15%. Thailand plant contributed only ~INR 2–3 cr revenue (just on stream). Pharma did >INR 50 cr last year.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue growth FY27:** **~15%** top-line (held from last call, despite +28% in Q1) — "difficult to predict quarterly" on war/freight/EO uncertainty; FY28 expected better on EO availability.
- **EBITDA margin:** 11.6% is now the **base/floor**; steady-state target **~15%+ consol** within ~2 years (once B2C exit + product-mix + utilisation mature).
- **Pharma:** target ~INR 70–75 cr FY27 (Chari; vs >INR 50 cr last year); CFO frames the *new*-pharma incremental potential at ~INR 30–50 cr this year; compliances (plant + customer) done by end Q2/Q3 → H2-weighted ramp.
- **B2C exit:** exit consumer/B2C (retain institutional cleaning); releases **2–3% EBITDA margin**; ~INR 50 cr debt tied to institutional+B2C.
- **Finance cost:** ~INR 9–10 cr/quarter run-rate going forward.
- **KSA greenfield:** ~**1.5 years** from formal announcement to first kilo of production; EO + non-EO mix; still WIP (survey/feedstock/land not finalised).
- **EO / capacity:** additional EO supply expected by ~Dec-2026 (end CY); MDEA continuous-ethoxylation plant ramp over next ~12 months → higher margins; EO capacity already ~100% utilised.
- **Long-range:** scale Rossari to **>2x** current revenue over the next ~4 years; exports maintained ~23–25%.
order book & pipeline: - Not an order-book model. Pipeline = capacity ramp (MDEA/ethoxylation, vitamin-premix plant, spray-cooled powders, biosurfactants, NMMO, fibre finishes — all "contributing handsomely" now), new Fibre Chemicals Division (fibre-to-fibre value chain), pharma & aroma molecules (H2 ramp), and geographic seeding (Thailand live, KSA WIP).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **HPPC:** crossed INR 550 cr quarterly; core growth engine (personal care, pharma applications, agrochemicals, performance chemicals); ethoxylation utilisation improving.
- **TSC:** ~+28%; launched **Fibre Chemicals Division** this quarter (integrated fibre-to-fibre solutions).
- **AHN:** ~+28%; new trace minerals, vitamin/enzyme premixes; vitamin-premix plant operational.
- **Institutional & B2C:** subdued, flat YoY, **loss-making** — the consol-margin drag; exiting the **consumer/B2C** part, keeping the more-profitable **institutional cleaning chemicals**; ~INR 50 cr debt attached.
- **Thailand (new):** small formulation/blending unit, INR 10–15 cr investment, on stream end of last quarter; Q1 rev ~INR 2–3 cr; textile products now, AHN/HPPC later; purpose = proximity to SE-Asia customers.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Pharma & aroma chemicals** — higher-margin; pharma ~INR 70–75 cr FY27 target, H2-weighted on compliance; the key margin-mix lever.
- **KSA greenfield** — access to globally competitive petrochemical feedstock/EO; strategic supply-side platform; ~1.5-yr gestation post-announcement; EO + non-EO.
- **MDEA / continuous ethoxylation ramp** — under-utilised, ~12-month ramp → margin uplift.
- **Non-EO chemistries (esters, NMMO, NMM/NFM, trace minerals)** — growth despite EO scarcity by shifting formulations to lower-EO / higher-non-EO content.
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- **EO access as a barrier:** India has a single (sole) EO supplier; Rossari's EO capacity is ~100% utilised and it holds an allocation relationship with a "very reputed, fair-pricing" corporate — a structural entry barrier for would-be surfactant competitors, though it caps Rossari's own EO-price negotiating power. (Supporting quote: "in India we have a sole supplier, so we do not have the opportunity to negotiate on our EO price… but the supplier is very reputed… fair in pricing, enabling us to remain globally competitive.")
- **Formulation/application R&D:** new integrated R&D centre + ability to re-engineer formulations toward non-EO content to keep growing when EO is scarce (evidenced this quarter) — a genuine applications-know-how edge.
margins & cost dynamics: - Consol EBITDA 11.6% (from 12.5% YoY); core-B2B ~14%. Drags: loss-making institutional/B2C tail, RM volatility (one-off ~INR 5 cr phenol hit from a delayed China shipment forcing spot buys; one mistimed RM block-buy), freight/insurance spikes (war-driven, vessel unavailability), and KSA/Thailand seeding costs. RM pass-through "no worry" over time but up-down volatility creates buyer hesitancy + timing losses. Path up: B2C exit (+2–3%), mix to pharma/aroma, capacity utilisation, MDEA ramp.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- **India capex deliberately slowed/calibrated** — only new products/molecules (pharma, aroma) get spend; priority is utilising the big FY23–26 investments. Term-loan interest now hitting P&L (capex commissioned) → higher finance cost, normalising to INR 9–10 cr/qtr.
- **Thailand:** INR 10–15 cr, live, ramping.
- **KSA:** only exploratory/pre-operational spend so far; plan intact; ~1.5-yr gestation post-announcement; in "deep discussions" with KSA ministry + feedstock suppliers.
- **Non-core monetisation:** Andheri office sold this Q (~INR 10.5 cr; Kanjurmarg ~INR 24 cr in Q4) — releasing capital.
capital allocation: - Net debt down INR 280 → 248 cr; focus on working-capital efficiency + cash generation. Monetising non-core real estate (2 offices in 2 quarters) to release capital toward higher-return areas. Capex calibrated (utilise-what's-built). B2C exit to simplify portfolio and lift RoCE/RoE. Will keep "seeding" market presence (exhibitions, customer visits) even at a short-term margin cost, given the >2x-in-4-years ambition — explicit that they won't starve growth to flatter EBITDA.
risks & watch-items:
- **Margin-recovery execution:** 15%+ steady-state is a 2-year, multi-step promise (B2C exit + mix + utilisation) — each step can slip.
- **EO single-supplier dependence:** ~100% utilised, no price-negotiation leverage; growth partly hostage to EO availability (more expected only ~Dec-2026).
- **RM / freight / geopolitical volatility:** phenol-type one-offs recur; war-driven freight/insurance spikes; RM-buying mistiming.
- **Pharma ramp is compliance-gated** (end Q2/Q3) and H2-loaded — timing risk.
- **KSA optionality is early** (nothing finalised) + West-Asia geopolitical overhang; seeding costs drag now.
- **PAT lag:** +4.5% vs EBITDA +18.7% — rising interest/depreciation as capex hits P&L.
management quality / tone: Confident, long-horizon, promoter-led tone (Menezes/Chari) balanced by a candid, numerate CFO (Sablok) who gave a clean margin bridge, the phenol one-off quantum, EO-utilisation reality, and honest "difficult to predict quarterly" hedging. Refreshingly disciplined on **not chasing quarterly optics** ("we will not stop seeding… just to show a slightly higher EBITDA margin") and on conservative FY27 guidance despite a 28% Q1. Some internal inconsistency on the pharma number (Chari INR 70–75 cr vs CFO INR 30–50 cr incremental) — flag to reconcile next quarter.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The 28% Q1 revenue growth is **~two-thirds price / one-third volume** (volume +10%) — so the "record quarter" is more RM-inflation pass-through than underlying demand; the maintained ~15% FY27 guide is the honest signal.
- **11.6% is being explicitly set as the margin floor** — a rare management "line in the sand" that becomes a clean verify-next-quarter test.
- **B2C exit is the single biggest margin lever** (2–3% EBITDA) and is portfolio-cleanup, not growth-sacrifice — core B2B already ~14–15%.
- EO being ~100% utilised + a sole national supplier is **both moat and ceiling** — the non-EO formulation pivot is how they keep growing until Dec-2026 EO relief.
- Non-core real-estate monetisation (2 offices in 2 quarters) is a quiet capital-release + RoCE story the P&L (only profit-element in other income) understates.

- **Formulation/application R&D:** new integrated R&D centre + ability to re-engineer formulations toward non-EO content to keep growing when EO is scarce (evidenced this quarter) — a genuine applications-know-how edge.
margins & cost dynamics: - Consol EBITDA 11.6% (from 12.5% YoY); core-B2B ~14%. - **Thailand:** INR 10–15 cr, live, ramping.
- **KSA:** only exploratory/pre-operational spend so far; plan intact; ~1.5-yr gestation post-announcement; in "deep discussions" with KSA ministry + feedstock suppliers.

capital allocation: - Net debt down INR 280 → 248 cr; focus on working-capital efficiency + cash generation. Monetising non-core real estate (2 offices in 2 quarters) to release capital toward higher-return areas. Capex calibrated (utilise-what's-built). B2C exit to simplify portfolio and lift RoCE/RoE. Will keep "seeding" market presence (exhibitions, customer visits) even at a short-term margin cost, given the >2x-in-4-years ambition — explicit that they won't starve growth to flatter EBITDA.
risks & watch-items:
- **Margin-recovery execution:** 15%+ steady-state is a 2-year, multi-step promise (B2C exit + mix + utilisation) — each step can slip.
- **EO single-supplier dependence:** ~100% utilised, no price-negotiation leverage; growth partly hostage to EO availability (more expected only ~Dec-2026).
- **RM / freight / geopolitical volatility:** phenol-type one-offs recur; war-driven freight/insurance spikes; RM-buying mistiming.
- **Pharma ramp is compliance-gated** (end Q2/Q3) and H2-loaded — timing risk.
- **KSA optionality is early** (nothing finalised) + West-Asia geopolitical overhang; seeding costs drag now.

management quality / tone: Confident, long-horizon, promoter-led tone (Menezes/Chari) balanced by a candid, numerate CFO (Sablok) who gave a clean margin bridge, the phenol one-off quantum, EO-utilisation reality, and honest "difficult to predict quarterly" hedging. Some internal inconsistency on the pharma number (Chari INR 70–75 cr vs CFO INR 30–50 cr incremental) — flag to reconcile next quarter.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The 28% Q1 revenue growth is **~two-thirds price / one-third volume** (volume +10%) — so the "record quarter" is more RM-inflation pass-through than underlying demand; the maintained ~15% FY27 guide is the honest signal.
- **11.6% is being explicitly set as the margin floor** — a rare management "line in the sand" that becomes a clean verify-next-quarter test.

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The global specialty chemicals industry is undergoing structural transformation driven by supply chain realignments, geopolitical shifts, stringent regulatory frameworks and an accelerating sustainable-chemistry mandate.
- 2025-26 was marked by geopolitical tensions, Red Sea logistics disruptions and freight fluctuations; textile tariff pressures led to cautious buying behaviour and strict collateral requirements from international buyers.
- Global conglomerates are aggressively de-risking supply chains, seeking partners offering backward integration and structural feedstock reliability.
- End-consumer habits are shifting rapidly — e.g. rising washing-machine penetration is driving a structural shift from powder to liquid detergents in home care; rising global meat consumption is accompanied by stricter food-safety demands in animal health.
- B2B customers increasingly require complex, proprietary blends and regulatory-compliant ingredients rather than commoditised single molecules.
- Global tariffs are pressuring margins for textile exporters and FMCG manufacturers, and customers are demanding 'chemistry plus service' — solutions that optimise the entire manufacturing cycle, not isolated chemical inputs.
- Customers (global FMCG and industrial brands) are seeking bio-based, zero-effluent and sustainable alternatives rather than merely passing environmental audits.
- International business contributed about 26% of consolidated revenue in FY26, growing 11% YoY, driven by deeper engagement with existing customers and expansion in Latin America, Europe, Southeast Asia and Africa.
- FY26 consolidated revenue growth of 15% was supported by healthy traction across businesses and steady progress in international markets, with all key divisions delivering healthy growth despite raw-material volatility and geopolitical disruption.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Rossari's FY26 capex programme centred on the Dahej cluster: an additional 20,000 MTPA capacity expansion at Dahej was commissioned effective 26th September 2025, taking total installed capacity to 2,72,500 MTPA (Directors' Report), while a 30,000 MTPA ethoxylation facility at Unitop's Dahej facility was commissioned in a phased manner across September 2025 and March 2026 and is in steady ramp-up, with fungible reactors being used to scale non-EO product lines amid near-term Ethylene Oxide supply constraints. Across the group, the Company capitalised approximately Rs 2,445 million during 2025-26 towards this capacity augmentation, funded through a mix of internal accruals and debt; the new Thailand blending unit was funded the same way. Internationally, the Company received in-principle approval to set up a greenfield manufacturing facility in KSA, strengthening regional access, supply-chain resilience and speed-to-market, subject to funding evaluation and statutory approvals. Manufacturing is spread across six named facilities — Dahej I (1,52,500 MTPA, 23 acres), Dahej II (90,000 MTPA, 22 acres), Silvassa (1,20,000 MTPA, 9 acres), Sarigam (15,000 MTPA, 2.5 acres), Vasai (600 MTPA, 0.27 acres) and Thailand (5,000 MTPA, 0.46 acres). With major capacity creation now in place, management's stated focus is shifting from capacity creation to capital efficiency — better asset utilisation, improved asset turns and integration-led efficiencies, supported by SAP S/4HANA and Salesforce.
